svg.title: Tang Nano 20K header pins as the oxrok logic analyzer uses them
svg.desc: Top view, USB connector up. Left header, top to bottom: CH0 73, CH1 74, trigger out 75, CH14 85, CH2 77, LEDs 15 and 16, CH3 27, CH4 28, 25 and 26 unused, CH5 29, CH6 30, CH7 31, LEDs 17, 20, 19, 18, 3V3, GND. Right header: 5V, GND, CH15 76, CH13 80, CH8 42, CH9 41, 56, 54 and 51 unused, CH10 48, 55, 49, 86 and 79 unused, GND, 3V3, CH11 72, CH12 71, 53 and 52 unused.
svg.text: top view, USB-C up; numbers are the labels printed on the board (FPGA pins); 3.3 V only
ADC CLK in the ADC build
Inputs have the FPGA's weak pull-down. CH13-CH15 share their pin with something on the board; the pins marked "not used" are driven or loaded by it.
